absent: How small block plug, unplug and removal helpers implement host coordination and guest page handling.
How fake offline and fake online transitions interact with guest memory onlining and migration.
Behavior of memory and power management notifier callbacks and device registration teardown.
Transport details of generic request submission, completion waiting and error propagation beyond the wakeup.
Initialization of work scheduling, retry timing and host response waiting before first use.
Defaults and valid ranges for module controls governing big block forcing, override sizing and online reaping.
Address translation helpers between physical spans and block identifiers and containment checks.
Dynamic memory group and parent resource interplay with operating system addition and removal paths.
Exact crash capture registration lifecycle and temporary range list ownership beyond allocation helpers.

findings.text: A shared helper establishes a device with exactly one queue, associating a caller supplied name and completion callback with that queue and propagating allocation failure as an error pointer.
A big region is considered offline only when none of its section sized slices currently backs an online page; any single online slice defeats the predicate.
A big region is considered movable when every online slice within it resides in the movable zone; slices without an online page are ignored rather than causing failure.

Big block retirement requires the added condition on entry, moves through a fake offline condition while guest pages are quiesced, and on full success reaches unused while a late host release failure leaves the plugged condition; any earlier failure restores added.

Retirement serializes guest onlining activity with the device hotplug mutex while marking fake offline status and while restoring prior status on failure; the later host facing removal and release steps run without holding that mutex.

Host driven shrinkage converts the byte delta into a whole count of big regions and reaps from the high end in three passes preferring fully offline regions, then fully movable regions, then any added region, skipping busy regions and stopping early when online reaping is disabled.

Eligibility probing during shrinkage intentionally runs without locks and may race with concurrent online or offline activity; the design treats stale eligibility as benign because the subsequent retirement revalidates state.
Plug management selects between small block and big block handling according to the active mode flag recorded at initialization, with unplug requests delegating to the matching implementation.

Periodic cleanup drives every lingering plugged unit toward unused by asking the host to release it first; small block mode additionally retries removal of partially unplugged units across movable and kernel and offline partial conditions.

Small block removal retries hold the hotplug mutex while attempting to drop fully unplugged operating system blocks, accumulate per block failures with a combined status, and defer further attempts by retaining a pending flag.

Configuration refresh reconciles the driver cached plugged amount with the device value, bounds the usable span by the smaller of device extent and pluggable extent, derives the last usable unit identifier from the inclusive end address with a downward adjustment for partial trailing units, and then reloads the requested amount.

The configuration area carries plugged_size and requested_size and usable_region_size; the driver treats the first as a reflection of its own prior actions and the second as the target to converge toward.

A work item drives convergence: it suppresses activity in crash capture kernels and when marked broken, honors a pending full release flag and a pending configuration change flag, cleans leftovers, then plugs or unplugs toward the requested amount.

Work completion maps result codes to distinct dispositions: success resets the backoff interval, address space exhaustion pauses without retry, transient resource pressure arms a timer, an explicit retry code reruns immediately, and any other code permanently marks the device broken.
Timer expiry requests another work pass and applies exponential backoff to the delay, bounded above by a configured maximum, with a one shot disposition.

Guest request queue completion wakes a host response wait channel associated with the device private data; initialization binds that handler to a single queue under a stable textual name and records the queue for later requests.
The guest request channel uses name guest-request; retry pacing is bounded below by VIRTIO_MEM_RETRY_TIMER_MIN_MS and above by VIRTIO_MEM_RETRY_TIMER_MAX_MS with doubling on each expiry.

Initialization chooses small block mode when the derived subblock extent is smaller than an operating system block and big block forcing is off; otherwise it chooses big block mode with an extent at least one operating system block, optionally enlarged by a power of two override.

The first usable unit identifier is rounded upward from the larger of device start and pluggable start, and the offline threshold is raised to cover at least two units so that growth remains possible.

Hotplug setup creates a parent resource, registers a dynamic group sized to one unit, then registers memory and power management callbacks and the device itself before marking readiness; failures unwind in reverse order.

Misaligned device start or end relative to operating system block extent, or any portion outside the pluggable span, does not abort probing but emits diagnostics and may leave edge memory unusable with later address space exhaustion.

Per device state groups addressing and sizing, mode specific block management with first and next and last usable identifiers, hotplug serialization, work scheduling with active and configuration change flags, retry timing, and crash capture caching.

The driver reserves the whole device span as exclusive system memory under a duplicated device name, then clears the busy indication so that later operating system addition can succeed; deletion releases the reservation and frees associated allocations idempotently.
Name duplication protects against stale pointers when the driver is force removed; failure to reserve warns that reloading is unsupported and aborts with a busy status.
Reservation uses IORESOURCE_SYSTEM_RAM together with IORESOURCE_EXCLUSIVE, then removes IORESOURCE_BUSY to present the span as available for managed addition.

State interrogation expresses the byte span as a count of device blocks, issues a state operation, returns the device reported condition on acknowledgement, maps device error to an invalid argument status, and otherwise reports allocation failure.

State queries use VIRTIO_MEM_REQ_STATE and interpret VIRTIO_MEM_RESP_ACK as success carrying VIRTIO_MEM_STATE_PLUGGED or VIRTIO_MEM_STATE_UNPLUGGED, while VIRTIO_MEM_RESP_ERROR denotes device rejection.
Crash capture page classification holds the hotplug mutex while aligning to device block granularity and while consulting or refreshing a single entry cache of the most recently queried block.

Addresses outside the device span are reported as ordinary memory, an empty device reports no device memory, and any interrogation failure is treated as absent memory rather than propagating an error.

Crash capture enumeration walks the usable span in chunks sized to the larger of section extent and device block extent, queries each chunk once, coalesces adjacent chunks containing any plugged portion, and appends the coalesced extents to the caller list.
Enumeration holds the hotplug mutex across the entire walk and stages results in a temporary list that is either spliced to the output on success or discarded on failure.

Device probing refuses operation without configuration access, loads immutable addressing and sizing and placement properties with a fallback node derivation, then diverges to crash capture registration when in capture mode or to full hotplug setup otherwise.

Capture mode marks readiness immediately so callbacks may arrive, registers page classification and optionally range enumeration handlers, disables hotplug messaging, and fails probing when capture support is unavailable.
Work execution is unexpected in capture kernels and returns after a one time diagnostic without touching device state; broken marking after an unrecognized status is terminal for subsequent passes.
Big block lifecycle distinguishes VIRTIO_MEM_BBM_BB_ADDED and VIRTIO_MEM_BBM_BB_FAKE_OFFLINE and VIRTIO_MEM_BBM_BB_PLUGGED and VIRTIO_MEM_BBM_BB_UNUSED for state tracking.

Small block lifecycle distinguishes VIRTIO_MEM_SBM_MB_PLUGGED and VIRTIO_MEM_SBM_MB_UNUSED and VIRTIO_MEM_SBM_MB_MOVABLE_PARTIAL and VIRTIO_MEM_SBM_MB_KERNEL_PARTIAL and VIRTIO_MEM_SBM_MB_OFFLINE_PARTIAL for state tracking.
Configuration layout provides device block extent and node placement and base address and total region extent alongside usable extent and plugged and requested amounts.
Work coordination tracks an active indication and a pending configuration change indication that are set and tested around each pass.
